newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on early Japanese buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on early Japanese buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended firmer on Tuesday compared to New York's Monday close on strong buying from Japan in early trade, dampened slightly by overseas sales in the afternoon session, bullion dealers said.
"Things drifted lower after the Japanese buying this morning," said one trader at an international bank.
Bullion ended at US$357.80/358.30 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$357.50/358.00 close on Monday.
Japanese traders were buying gold on a weaker dollar/yen, bullion dealers said this morning. But European sales in afternoon trade depressed the market, traders said.
Some traders reported small amounts of short covering, but on the whole the market was seen softening further before staging a recovery.

"There will be a bounce, there will be quite a sharp recovery, but where it's going to come from remains to be seen," Dick Gazmararian, executive vice president of precious metals in the Asia Pacific for Republic National Bank, told Reuters.
Local gold ended HK$24 lower at HK$3,309 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.00 from -4.00
Tael gold was trading at a premium to spot gold, with the U.S. equivalent at $358.90 per ounce.
